events.title: FOMC decision, SEP/dot plot, Warsh press conference
events.why_it_matters: Markets price ~92-95% odds of a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%, the first under Chair Warsh; the SEP/dots and presser matter more than the move itself.
events.what_to_watch: Median 2026-27 dots, any signal of a second hike, and whether Warsh frames energy inflation as a one-off or a persistent regime.

events.title: August advance retail sales rebound +0.6% MoM
events.why_it_matters: Sales recovered after July's -0.6% drop, softening the pre-Fed stagflation narrative even as energy inflation and a near-certain hike still dominate.
events.what_to_watch: Control-group/core retail detail versus gasoline and autos; whether the rebound survives later revisions.

events.title: Japan August trade deficit widens on oil imports
events.why_it_matters: The deficit hit about ¥1.11tn, the fourth straight shortfall, as crude import values jumped ~59% YoY even while chip and auto exports stayed strong.
events.what_to_watch: Whether oil-driven import bills plus a likely BoJ hike accelerate yen-carry unwind into Friday's decision.

events.title: Lennar Q3 earnings (housing bellwether)
events.why_it_matters: Mega-cap earnings are quiet this week, so Lennar is the main read-through on orders, incentives, and margins as mortgage rates and 10-year yields sit near 5%.
events.what_to_watch: New orders, cancellation rate, ASP/incentives, and FY guidance versus consensus EPS ~$1.28–$1.32.

events.title: US-China talks on targeted tariff cuts ahead of Xi visit
events.why_it_matters: Bloomberg reports reciprocal cuts on roughly $30bn of energy, agriculture, and manufacturing inputs as Bessent prepares to meet He Lifeng this weekend.
events.what_to_watch: Whether talks produce a written truce-extension framework before the Sept 24 summit, or stall on Taiwan/AI/export controls.

events.title: Bank of England decision — hold at 3.75% expected
events.why_it_matters: A Reuters poll was unanimous for a hold, but oil-driven inflation risk has lifted hike odds to ~27-30% and a hawkish 6-3 split plus slower QT remain live.
events.what_to_watch: Vote split versus July's 6-3, QT pace, and Bailey's language on second-round energy effects.

events.title: Bank of Japan decision — hike to 1.25% widely expected
events.why_it_matters: A 25bp hike to a 31-year high, landing a day after a hawkish Fed, is the classic yen-carry unwind trigger as oil imports already blow out the trade deficit.
events.what_to_watch: Ueda's guidance on the pace of further hikes and any language on FX/financial stability.

events.title: US August housing starts and building permits
events.why_it_matters: Existing-home sales already fell to a 2026 low; starts/permits will show whether higher mortgage rates are freezing new construction as well.
events.what_to_watch: Single-family starts versus multifamily, and permits as the leading rate-sensitive signal.

events.title: SEMICON India 2026 (New Delhi)
events.why_it_matters: Modi-hosted gathering of leading chipmakers is a supply-chain/capex signal as AI demand stays hot and geopolitics push diversification away from single-node risk.
events.what_to_watch: Capex, packaging, and incentive announcements from foundry/OSAT and equipment vendors.

events.title: Holtec Nuclear IPO (HNUC) — ~$825M nuclear listing
events.why_it_matters: One of the largest energy IPOs of the window, priced off AI-driven power demand and Palisades restart/SMR-300 plans, into a hawkish-rate tape.
events.what_to_watch: Final pricing versus $15–$18 range, first-day float, and whether dual-class voting discounts the deal.

events.title: Electra Therapeutics IPO (ETRA)
events.why_it_matters: Largest biotech IPO in the window (~$325–$347M) tests risk appetite for clinical-stage names after a cluster of FDA approvals.
events.what_to_watch: Pricing versus $14–$16 and aftermarket demand if rates/volatility spike post-Fed/BoJ.

events.title: PBOC September LPR fix — hold expected
events.why_it_matters: 1y/5y LPRs sit at 3.00%/3.50% while credit demand is collapsing; a hold after Pan Gongsheng downplayed the loan slump would confirm Beijing is not rushing a big easing.
events.what_to_watch: Any surprise cut, or accompanying RRR/relending steps if activity data keep missing.

events.title: UNGA 81 high-level debate; Trump speech window
events.why_it_matters: Heads-of-state week overlaps the Xi visit and Iran/IAEA track; Trump remarks on Hormuz, China, and Ukraine can move oil, defense, and tariff-sensitive names.
events.what_to_watch: Any ceasefire/Hormuz language, Iran nuclear demands, and side meetings with Xi, Zelenskyy, or Gulf leaders.

events.title: AutoZone Q4 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Best high-frequency read on US consumer trade-down and DIY auto spend into a rate-hike/oil-shock tape.
events.what_to_watch: SSS, gross margin, and commentary on lower-income traffic versus ticket size.

events.title: Trump-Xi Washington state visit/summit
events.why_it_matters: Highest-stakes trade event of the quarter: tariffs, AI, Taiwan arms, and the Iran war, less than six weeks before US midterms and with the Nov 10 truce expiry looming.
events.what_to_watch: Truce extension language, any Taiwan/arms-sale freeze, and commercial packages (ag, energy, Boeing) versus a walk-away.

events.title: Costco Q4 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Membership-club bellwether for middle-income spending power as gasoline, rates, and food inflation squeeze real incomes.
events.what_to_watch: Traffic vs ticket, membership-fee commentary, and inventory/gross-margin mix.

events.title: US August new home sales
events.why_it_matters: Confirms whether builders can still move inventory with incentives after existing-home sales hit a 2026 low and the 10-year sits at 5%.
events.what_to_watch: Months of supply, median price, and South/West regional splits.

events.title: US-China trade truce expires November 10 — pre-summit positioning
events.why_it_matters: The one-year pause on heightened reciprocal tariffs and many Section 301 exclusions ends Nov 10; Sept 24 is the last realistic leader-level window to extend it.
events.what_to_watch: Extension length, exclusion list, and whether fentanyl/tech controls are bundled into any deal.

events.title: US-Canada Section 338 import bans take effect
events.why_it_matters: 50% Section 338 duties already apply; on Sept 29 selected Canadian alcohol, dairy, and some vehicle categories shift from tariff to outright import prohibition.
events.what_to_watch: Last-minute list changes, Canadian counter-tariff escalation, and any USMCA/CUSMA negotiation restart.

events.title: August JOLTS (job openings)
events.why_it_matters: Labor-demand check after August payrolls beat at +162k and unemployment held 4.1%; a hot openings print would validate hiking into oil shock.
events.what_to_watch: Openings level, quits rate, and openings-to-unemployed ratio versus post-NFP revisions.

events.title: August PCE inflation (Fed's preferred gauge) + Q2 GDP third estimate
events.why_it_matters: Consensus clusters near ~0.3% MoM / ~3.8% YoY headline PCE and ~0.24–0.30% MoM / ~3.3% YoY core; a hot print after a hike would keep a second move live into Q4.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE vs 3.3% and whether BEA annual revisions mechanically lower YoY; GDP third estimate is secondary.

events.title: US-Iran tanker war; Brent ~$107–108, Hormuz impaired
events.why_it_matters: Tit-for-tat tanker strikes and curtailed Hormuz flows keep Brent near $107–108, feeding global energy CPI and forcing G3 central banks hawkish.
events.what_to_watch: Transit volumes, insurance premia, East-West pipeline status, and any UNGA de-escalation language.

events.title: 10-year Treasury yield holds ~5% — global duration shock
events.why_it_matters: The 10-year is still pinned near 5.00% after last week's breach, a direct valuation headwind for long-duration equities, housing, and utilities into the Fed.
events.what_to_watch: Post-FOMC/BoJ yield reaction and whether 5% becomes a new range floor rather than a spike.

events.title: August CPI — energy spike plus core MoM beat locked in hike
events.why_it_matters: Headline +0.4% MoM / 3.4% YoY with gasoline +3.9% and core +0.3% MoM (beat vs ~0.2%) pushed FedWatch hike odds into the 90s.
events.what_to_watch: How Warsh treats energy as transitory vs embedded; next CPI is Oct 14.

events.title: August PPI — final demand +0.4% MoM, +5.4% YoY
events.why_it_matters: Wholesale inflation hit 2026 highs as diesel jumped 24.1% MoM, confirming the oil shock is already in the pipeline before PCE.
events.what_to_watch: Pass-through into September goods CPI and core PCE services.

events.title: ECB 25bp hike delivered; hawkish forecast upgrade
events.why_it_matters: Deposit rate to 2.50% effective today; staff raised 2027-28 inflation and 2026-27 growth, explicitly citing Middle East energy inflation.
events.what_to_watch: Whether markets price another hike after US/BoJ this week; next ECB is after this window.

events.title: China August activity — IP beats, retail and FAI miss
events.why_it_matters: IP +5.2% YoY beat, but retail +0.4% missed and Jan-Aug FAI contracted 7.2%, keeping stimulus hopes alive and weighing on global cyclicals.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the Sept 24 summit or LPR week produces fiscal/credit follow-through.

events.title: China August credit — new loans far below consensus
events.why_it_matters: New yuan loans were only +60bn yuan vs ~400bn expected; outstanding loan growth slowed to a record-low 4.9% YoY with household loans still contracting.
events.what_to_watch: Pan's 'unfazed' stance versus any quiet RRR/relending if September credit stays dead.

events.title: OPEC+ holds October quotas; next review Oct 4
events.why_it_matters: Core OPEC+ left October output unchanged after finishing the 1.65mbpd voluntary-cut rollback, offering no offset to Hormuz disruption.
events.what_to_watch: Oct 4 eight-country meeting and 2027 capacity-baseline talks later this year.

events.title: IAEA refers Iran to UN Security Council
events.why_it_matters: First NPT-safeguards referral in 20 years (23-3-8) raises sanctions/escalation risk even if China/Russia can veto new UNSC penalties.
events.what_to_watch: UNSC handling this month and Iranian retaliation risk around Hormuz/nuclear sites.

events.title: Google ad-tech remedies: no AdX breakup
events.why_it_matters: Judge Brinkema rejected DOJ's structural remedy, another liability-without-breakup outcome that reduces Big Tech legal-tail risk.
events.what_to_watch: Sealed opinion details and any appeal; behavioral access/pricing rules still pending final judgment.

events.title: DOJ probe of Nvidia–Groq licensing/acquihire
events.why_it_matters: Antitrust review of the ~$17–20bn Groq license/talent deal tests whether AI 'non-deals' can dodge HSR — a sector-wide template risk.
events.what_to_watch: Scope of information requests and any fine vs unwind talk; unwind is considered unlikely.

events.title: August payrolls +162k beat; unemployment 4.1%
events.why_it_matters: Jobs rebounded well above ~55k consensus, giving Warsh cover to hike despite oil-driven inflation rather than ease into weakness.
events.what_to_watch: Next employment report is Oct 2; JOLTS on Sept 29 is the interim labor check.

events.title: Existing-home sales fall to 2026 low
events.why_it_matters: Sales at 3.98mn SAAR (-2.0% MoM) with 4.9 months' supply confirm housing is freezing as the 10-year and mortgage rates grind higher.
events.what_to_watch: Starts (Sept 17), new-home sales (Sept 24), and post-Fed mortgage-rate move.

events.title: US-mediated Ukraine talks revived; October round possible
events.why_it_matters: Witkoff/Kushner shuttle to Moscow and Kyiv reopened a trilateral track, but territorial gaps remain and fighting continues.
events.what_to_watch: UNGA side meetings and whether Kyiv's October-talks prep produces a venue/date.

events.title: Congress CR funds government through Dec 11 — shutdown risk off
events.why_it_matters: The Sept 30 FY-end cliff is already patched; next fight is a post-midterm Dec 11 deadline, and the debt limit is not live until 2027.
events.what_to_watch: Lame-duck appropriations tone after November elections — not this window.

top_risks: Hawkish Warsh SEP/dots plus a BoJ hike trigger a synchronized G3 tightening and yen-carry unwind while the 10-year is already ~5%.
Iran tanker war / Hormuz disruption keeps Brent ~$107+ and turns a 'one-off' energy shock into persistent core inflation.
Trump-Xi summit fails to extend the Nov 10 tariff truce, or Taiwan/arms-sale friction cancels/hollows the visit.
US-Canada Section 338 bans on Sept 29 escalate a North American goods war into autos, food, and industrials.
China credit/demand slump deepens with no LPR/fiscal offset, hitting global cyclicals and commodities into year-end.
top_opportunities: Targeted US-China tariff cuts and a truce extension around Sept 24 would be the clearest risk-on catalyst for trade-sensitive cyclicals and ag/energy exporters.
A Warsh presser that hikes but signals one-and-done (energy treated as transitory) could rally duration and rate-sensitive equities after the 5% yield shock.
Any credible Hormuz de-escalation at UNGA would crush the oil risk premium and ease the stagflation overlay.
Nuclear/AI-power (Holtec IPO) and semiconductor diversification (SEMICON India) remain structural bid stories if rates stabilize.
Housing-related oversold names could bounce if Lennar/starts show incentives working and the Fed does not hike the 2027 dots aggressively.
summary: Today is a regime day: retail sales already rebounded +0.6%, but the 2pm ET FOMC/SEP/Warsh presser is still ~90%+ priced as the first hike of the Warsh Fed, with BoE Thursday and a widely expected BoJ hike to 1.25% Friday. The overlay is stagflationary — Brent still ~$107 on the US-Iran tanker war, the 10-year pinned near 5%, and China demand remaining weak — while the Sept 24 Trump-Xi summit is the main two-way event for tariffs and risk appetite.
